item.title: The secret economics inside the new Planet Money board game
item.description: From Nobel Prize-winning research to the Laffer Curve, Scabby the Rat, Veblen's peacock, and more — the economic ideas and inside jokes hiding throughout Planet Money's new board game.

item.title: Does spending money make you feel bad? Read this comic
item.description: If spending — or not spending — money makes you feel shame or regret, you might be grappling with financial guilt. Financial planner Lauryn Williams breaks down three types and how to deal.

item.description: CEOs of the country's two biggest theater chains say they support the merger of Paramount-Skydance with Warner Brothers-Discovery.

item.title: How FIFA President Gianni Infantino reached the pinnacle of power in soccer
item.description: Gianni Infantino is facing intense heat over a failed plan to privatize the World Cup. He is a lawyer who rose to the pinnacle of soccer and is now trying to hold onto his job.

item.title: Selling experiences, not things: Services overtake physical goods in downtown retail
item.description: America's downtowns are changing. Storefronts that used to showcase clothes or gifts are giving way to gyms and salons. Last year marked the first time that more retail space went to shops offering services rather than things.

item.title: Trump renews push to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook
item.description: Trump is once again threatening to fire Cook over unproven allegations of mortgage fraud after an earlier effort to remove Cook was struck down by the Supreme Court.

item.title: Employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs in a sign of a wilting labor market
item.description: U.S. employers cut 23,000 jobs in July, and job gains for the two previous months were weaker than initially reported, according to a report Friday from the Labor Department.

item.title: Amid cost of living stress, many parents are supporting children well into adulthood
item.description: Polls show most Americans think young adults today have it harder financially than past generations. A majority of parents help their grown children with expenses, even if it hurts their own finances.
